goalNotes: Aino's main goal stat would be Elemental Mastery to maximize her reaction damage and Elemental Burst scaling. Energy Recharge to ensure consistent Burst uptime.
Optional stats after EM and ER are CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG to help her reaction damage to scale a little higher.

recommendedTeams.name: Aino Lunar Charged Team
notes: Aino is a strong support for Lunar Charged teams with her Elemental Burst, especially when paired with a Lunar-Charged support like Ineffa.
The best beneficiary unit for this would be Flins as both are Nod-Krai characters and Flins benefits from having a Hydro support that can trigger his Lunar Charge.

recommendedTeams.name: Aino Lunar-Crystallize Team
notes: Aino can serve as the Hydro applicator in Lunar-Crystallize teams with Zibai or Linnea available, as they can enable Lunar-Crystallize as reaction for Aino to amplify.

recommendedTeams.name: Aino Bloom Teams
notes: Aino has good synergy with Bloom teams as she provides enough Hydro application to trigger the reaction.
Alongside another Hydro unit and Dendro unit like Nahida and Nilou, the team can consistently deal a good amount of damage.

recommendedTeams.name: Aino-Arlecchino Vaporize Team
notes: Aino is a solid support option in Arlecchino teams thanks to her slower Hydro application, which allows Arlecchino to consistently trigger Vaporize without overwriting the Pyro aura.
She also provides utility as a Nod-Krai unit, enabling access to Nod-Krai set bonuses and additional team buffs.

goalNotes: Albedo's damage starts reaching the upper limit once he goes past 2,000 DEF, with 2,300 being a good stopping point. However, if playing him entirely for his Hexerei buffs, then getting his DEF to 3000 should be a priority to maximize buff potency.

CRIT Rate is next on the priority list with 60% as a baseline, as you want to make sure that all instances of his damage have an increased chance to land CRIT hits. Any remaining substats should go to CRIT DMG.

recommendedTeams.name: Albedo Hexerei Teams
notes: In order to utilize his Hexerei Teams, you must include another Hexerei member to access his additional combat abilities. With his buffs, he's a general Sub-DPS that can be slotted in any team as long you satisfied the caveat of the buffs. He doesn't shine in a particular team but he does offer an all-around buff for his teammates.

recommendedTeams.name: Albedo Mono Geo Teams
notes: Mono-Geo team comps are Albedo's best teams to utilize the Geo Resonance. He also serves as a battery for Geo characters with high energy requirements like Itto and Gorou.

recommendedTeams.name: Albedo Double Geo Teams
notes: Double Geo teams allow Albedo's Sub-DPS capabilities to shine with paired with a support like Zhongli, who offers both geo resonance and a resistance-shredding shield.
Combining them with other potent duos such as Hu Tao and Xingqiu can make for a well-rounded team, especially when they can make use of Albedo's Elemental Mastery increase from his Elemental Burst.

recommendedTeams.name: Albedo Rainbow Teams
notes: Rainbow teams that can have an additional slot for Albedo is decent enough as it provides free off-field DPS at no cost whatsover. His Elemental Mastery buff on his burst is also good for teams that have transformative reactions such as Vaporize or Electro-Charged.

recommendedTeams.name: Alhaitham Quickbloom Teams
notes: This Alhaitham team comp focuses on applying as much Dendro as possible to cause or trigger a combination of Hyperbloom and Quicken. The Dendro in this team can be substituted with another Electro if you have enough Energy Recharge for Alhaitham.
If you do not have Nahida, Raiden, or Yelan, a more free to play option with Yaoyao, Xingqiu, and Shinobu are also good.
Alhaitham Best Team Comps

recommendedTeams.name: Alhaitham Furina Teams
notes: Furina is one of Alhaitham's best supports when it comes to increasing his damage, and perfectly slots into a traditional Alhaitham quickbloom team albeit losing out on some Hydro Application.
The tradeoff is worth it however, as the buffs that Furina offers in exchange for a lack of comfort can significantly increase the overall damage output of the team.

recommendedTeams.name: Alhaitham Spread Teams
notes: A party consisting of Dendro and Electro characters enables Alhaitham to focus on maximizing his own personal damage with Spread. Other supprortive characters like Zhongli, or buffers for Electro like Kazuha are okay alternatives.

recommendedTeams.name: Alhaitham Burgeon Teams
notes: This team comp for Alhaitham centers around him enabling the formation of cores for Thoma to trigger Bugeon. For the reaction to not cause Burning, two Hydro Characters (or an Anemo to swirl Hydro) are recommended to facilitate the reaction.

recommendedTeams.name: Alhaitham Free-to-Play Teams
notes: If you don't have premium characters, this free-to-play party that centers on Hyperbloom or Quicken can perform well for Alhaitham. Lisa, however, will need a lot of Energy Recharge to make her accessible.

recommendedTeams.name: Amber Burst Support
notes: Amber's supportive role focuses on her soaking up enemy aggro with Baron Bunny and applying Pyro for units that can take advantage of them, such as Kazuha in a Hu Tao team for the Viridescent Venerer shred, and Lyney.

recommendedTeams.name: Amber Melt / Burst DPS
notes: This team takes advantage of Cryo applications, as well as Bennett's buffs to enable Amber to deal a good amount of Melt DMG.
This can either be played via a prolonged Charged Shot playstyle, or by detonating two of her Baron Bunnies as a Frontloaded DPS.

goalNotes: Arlecchino values as much ATK and CRIT in her stats as much as possible, with an emphasis on CRIT Rate in order for her to deal increased damage with her Pyro-infused Normal Attacks.
ATK and CRIT DMG are then to be taken as far as you can go with them, with her ATK benefitting the most at 2,000 and her CRIT DMG being at 160% and above if possible.

recommendedTeams.name: Arlecchino DPS Teams
notes: Arlecchino has access to multiple team compositions such as Vaporize, Melt, Overload, Burning, and Mono-Pyro. All she requires in these teams are elemental reaction-enablers to boost her own DMG, and some form of buffing to improve her DMG, or sustain options like interruption resistance to keep her attacks going at a steady pace.

recommendedTeams.name: Arlecchino F2P Teams
notes: These are a similar set of teams for Arlecchino, but made to be more F2P-friendly. Bring Xingqiu and Candace for a Vaporize team, Rosaria and Diona for Melt, Collei and Sucrose for Burn, or Xiangling and Sucrose for Mono-Pyro. Overload F2P Variant Overload is primarily composed of 4-star units already, so it is not listed here since the team comp is relatively the same as the one in her premium team list.

recommendedTeams.name: Arlecchino-Varesa Dual Teams
notes: This dual dps team archetype is an offshoot of both of their Overload teams. It primarily make use of Arlecchino's Blood-Debt Due wait time by using Varesa to do her combos. Varesa is the one to keep Iansan's Kinetic Energy at a certain level before switching to Arlecchino to do frontload damage.

recommendedTeams.name: Ayaka Freeze Teams
notes: Freeze teams are among one of Ayaka's best use cases as she can constantly keep opponents frozen in place while dealing high single target and AoE damage.

recommendedTeams.name: Ayaka F2P Team Comp
notes: This Ayaka F2P team will require her to get very close to enemies to apply the Wet status from Barbara's Elemental Skill. Kaeya will help refill Ayaka's Elemental Burst while the Anemo Traveler can slightly help with grouping enemies together.

goalNotes: Ayato wants to reach around 2,000 ATK as the standard baseline for most ATK-based DPS units. However, he can also derive some of his ATK stats from his HP, which get converted to ATK.

Afterwards, focus on maintaining at least 70% CRIT Rate and around 160% or more CRIT DMG to ensure that he outputs meaningful and consistent damage. His Energy Recharge can either be left alone, or taken to around 130% if you want to use his Burst every rotation.

recommendedTeams.name: Ayato Rainbow Teams
notes: Ayato will be the trigger in this Electro-Charged plus Vaporize team. Fischl (especially at C6) can help recharge Ayato's energy while Bennett can boost Ayato's damage and heal the party.
Make sure to swirl Pyro first by using Kazuha's burst while standing on Bennett's burst for Kazuha to self-swirl Pyro!

recommendedTeams.name: Ayato Vaporize Teams
notes: Ayato can achieve his highest personal DPS by triggering Vaporize reactions during his Elemental Skill.
This usually requires two Pyro units in order to be consistent with Vaporizes, but a second or third Pyro unit can be swapped out for an Anemo unit who can swirl Pyro and keep up Pyro uptime.

recommendedTeams.name: Ayato Hyperbloom Teams
notes: Ayato is also a great enabler for the Hyperbloom reaction. His Elemental Skill will help create Dendro Cores while the off-field Electro Character will trigger the Hyperbloom reaction.

recommendedTeams.name: Ayato Burgeon Teams
notes: This Dendro Team Comp for Ayato will only need 2 core teammates, a Pyro and Dendro off-field damage dealer. The goal is to create Dendro Cores by using Ayato and the Dendro Traveler's Elemental Burst. Afterwards, the off-field Pyro unit will trigger the Burgeon reaction with Pyro damage.
Afterwards, you can swap Ayato back in and do damage with his Elemental Skill.

recommendedTeams.name: Ayato Freeze Teams
notes: With the addition of more damage-increasing supports for Freeze, Ayato has new teammates such as Furina and Escoffier to pair with in Freeze teams, allowing him to keep up his damage.

recommendedTeams.name: Ayato F2P Teams
notes: For newer players, a Hyperbloom team comp can be used as an early game option for Ayato. You may opt to using Collei as well!

recommendedTeams.name: Sub-DPS Ayato Team
notes: Use Ayato's Elemental Burst to buff Yoimiya's Normal Attacks. He can also use his Elemental Skill to trigger Yoimiya's burst, while Bennett and Kazuha can further buff her! Note that Ayato will be the one Vaporizing in this team comp due to poor application.
Yoimiya can be replaced with Raiden Shogun or by any character who would appreciate the Hydo DMG Ayato provides with his Elemental burst.

recommendedTeams.name: Baizhu Hyperbloom Teams
notes: This Baizhu team is focused on triggering Hyperbloom to buff the reaction while off-field. We recommend bringing a second dendro to get resonance for the Elemental Mastery buff. Some of teams above can also combine Quicken to add damage.
Dendro Element and Reactions Guide

recommendedTeams.name: Baizhu Aggravate/Spread Teams
notes: Baizhu can replace Zhongli in Quicken teams, as well as cover a Dendro slot for you to add in another Electro or Dendro. Triple Dendro teams with Alhaitham and Nahida is also viable as long as you have an effective Electro applicator like Yae Miko.

recommendedTeams.name: Baizhu Burgeon Team
notes: Burgeon teams with Baizhu covers up the healing from the self-inflicted explosions as well as applying the Dendro while off-field. Baizhu can also act as a solo Dendro driver if he's the Main DPS in the party.

recommendedTeams.name: Baizhu Burning Team
notes: Baizhu acts both as a great shielder and dendro enabler in Burning teams, which would greatly benefit Kinich and Emilie. Similar to Burgeon teams, he can protect and heal the whole team from self-inflicted damage caused by Pyro.

recommendedTeams.name: Baizhu in Nilou Bloom Teams
notes: Baizhu provides healing for Nilou Bloom team comps, which frees characters like Kokomi, Barbara, or Yaoyao for other teams.
Best Team Comp | Party Building Guide

recommendedTeams.name: Barbara Dendro Core Teams
notes: Barbara Dendro Core teams focuses on Barbara generating Dendro Cores in tandem with her Dendro allies. With fridge teams, there is the added benefit of freezing enemies in place, allowing bloom cores to reliably pop around them.

recommendedTeams.name: Barbara Support Role
notes: Barbara as a support can be fitted in any team comp. She applies very little Hydro through her Elemental Skill, which can help in not interfering with other Elemental Reactions.
In this team comp we have Barbara as a support and the second Hydro unit just so we can enable the Hydro Resonance, which will increase Yelan's damage.

recommendedTeams.name: Beidou Taser Team
notes: This team specializes in taking out multiple enemies with the Electo-charged reaction. Beidou provides Electro thanks to her Elemental Burst so that Tartaglia can trigger Electro-charged and deal tons of AoE DMG.

recommendedTeams.name: Beidou Stellar-Conduct Team
notes: Beidou can either serve as the On-Field or Off-Field Electro member in a Stellar-Conduct team so long as they have a reaction enabler or Main DPS like Sandrone.
Qiqi can be used as the better option as opposed to Diona in this team comp if she is available.

recommendedTeams.name: Beidou Hyperbloom Team
notes: While Beidou won't be participating in activating Dendro Cores for Hyperbloom, Beidou still acts as an Electro supplement to trigger Quicken to increase Hyperbloom DMG.

recommendedTeams.name: Beidou F2P Team
notes: This is Beidou's best team without any 5-star characters. A combination of Beidou and Xingqiu's Elemental Bursts combined with Fischl's Oz and Sucrose's Swirl through her Normal Attacks allows you to deal a lot of Electro-charged DMG in the process!

goalNotes: Bennett's main priority is to get his Energy Recharge to 200% or more, with that requirement lowering if he has Favonius Sword.

Afterwards, all of his substats can go into CRIT and ATK to boost his own damage whenever he uses his Elemental Burst or Skill, looking for at least 50 - 60% CRIT Rate, and around 150% CRIT DMG or more.

recommendedTeams.name: Hypercarry Support Teams
notes: While Bennett can serve as an ATK-buffer for almost every unit that scales off ATK, his most effective niche is that of a hypercarry support, with niche pivots as a multi-DPS support such as Hexerei teams. Mavuika, Varesa, Arlecchino, and Lyney are good examples of DPS units that are mainly the sole damage dealers of their team, making use of Bennett's buffs more easily.

recommendedTeams.name: Xiangling-Duo Teams
notes: Bennett has special synergy with Xiangling, who is able to use her Elemental Burst while in his buff circle, and be able to take that buff with her even off-field through the concept of Snapshotting. Because of this, Xiangling is one of the few characters that Bennett can pair with seamlessly, serving as a DPS-Support duo package for any team that can utilize them, such as Tartaglia and Raiden teams.

recommendedTeams.name: Bloom Team
notes: This team build focuses on the synergy of Candace and Yaoyao's Elemental Burst. Nilou will provide the aura that gives off Bountiful Cores, while Yaoyao with Hydro infusion can spread a lot of Dendro to enemies while mitigating Dendro DMG taken from the cores.

recommendedTeams.name: Electro-Charged Team
notes: This Candace team build focuses on triggering Electro-Charged elemental reactions. Cyno works particularly well with Candace since she can increase his Elemental Normal Attack damage without overriding his Electro Infused normal attacks.

recommendedTeams.name: Vaporize Team
notes: Candace can act as an enabler for Vaporize teams with her off-field Hydro DMG, especially at C6. In combination with Yun Jin, they will both enhance the Elemental Normal Attacks of the Main DPS!

recommendedTeams.name: Charlotte Freeze Teams
notes: Charlotte's magnificent Cryo application and AoE will work wonders in Freeze teams, provided that you can keep Hydro propped up. Yelan and Xingqiu will be able to do this no problem.
Additionally, putting Charlotte in a team filled with Fontanians like Wriothesley, Neuvillette, and Furina will be able to take advantage of her Passive Talent!

recommendedTeams.name: Freeze-Hyperbloom Teams
notes: If you wish to still take advantage of one of the strongest Elemental Reactions in the game, then having Charlotte co-exist in Hyperbloom teams will add several reactions into the mix, which theoretically can still co-exist due to Charlotte's slow but consistent periodic application.

goalNotes: Chasca's main priority is to stack up at least 40% CRIT Rate for comfortable crits when in Nightsoul's blessing, and around 200% CRIT DMG or more in order to ensure that she deals substantial damage.

recommendedTeams.name: Chasca Rainbow Teams
notes: These teams consist of Chasca mixed with exactly three other elements to give her Elemental Skill the most amount of differing bullets, allowing Chasca to trigger as many Elemental Reactions as possible.
This build sees more value if Chasca is on-field as the Anemo Driver for these reactions, as this allows her to create more instances of different reactions as she swirls them.

recommendedTeams.name: Chasca Melt Teams
notes: Chasca can serve as a great driver for Melt teams given the sheer damage multipliers it provides, especially now with Cryo options like Citlali and Escoffier.
In these teams, Chasca can decide whether they want two Cryo teammates or two Pyro teammates in order to pivot the team into being Melt or Reverse Melt.

recommendedTeams.name: Chasca Vaporize Teams
notes: Chasca can also make use of the Vaporize reaction with her Elemental Conversion, which helps trigger both ends of Vaporize as well as Swirl it around.

This also has the added benefit of giving Chasca access to either Furina, Bennett, or even Xilonen if Chasca uses a Pyro DMG Bonus Goblet, which helps in ensuring that her own personal damage is still respectable.

recommendedTeams.name: Chasca Electro-Charged Teams
notes: With Chasca's Elemental Conversion, she can facilitate the Electro-Charged reaction together with Ororon and other Electro and Hydro units as her bullets will be able to swirl and trigger the reaction.
In addition, Lunar-Charged only drives this reaction forward as it becomes more powerful in Chasca's hands with the addition of Lunar units like Ineffa and Columbina.

recommendedTeams.name: Chasca Overload Teams
notes: Chasca can also slot into Overload teams as her bullets can lock onto targets and trigger Overload with almost every hit when paired with allies with high Elemental application.

This is especially good with Chasca as the main DPS with her Elemental Skill's lock-on mechanic, which counters the innate possibility of Overload units accidentally splitting up their opponents in a fight.

goalNotes: Chevreuse wants to reach as close to 40,000 HP as possible in order to max out the ATK increase from her passive. Afterwards, the rest of her stats should go into Energy Recharge to let her cast her Elemental Burst off cooldown.

recommendedTeams.name: Chevreuse Raiden Hypercarry Team
notes: In Raiden's Hypercarry teams, Chevreuse replaces Kazuha for the ATK buffs and Electro RES Shred. This in combination with Sara and Bennett buffs, Raiden Shogun's damage should skyrocket more or less at a similar height!
If your Raiden is not at C2, then you may want to swap out Sara for another damage dealer like Xiangling.

recommendedTeams.name: Chevreuse Clorinde Overloaded Team
notes: Clorinde also thrives with Chevreuse's Overloaded comps so long as you have these two types of characters: an energy-giving Sub-DPS like Fischl or Raiden, a defensive that can help with interruption resistance like Thoma or Dehya.
If you have no issues with dodging attacks, you may also substitute your defensive supports for someone like Sara or Bennett.

recommendedTeams.name: Chevreuse Yoimiya Overloaded Team
notes: Yoimiya is one of the best partners for Chevreuse as the knockback effect from the Overloaded reaction isn't a big issue with her ranged attacks. Chevreuse essentially works as the support buffer for this team.

For your party members, you may use a combination of Raiden, Fischl, Beidou, Yae Miko, or Sara for Electro, but you can still have one more Pyro with Bennett or Thoma should you wish to give her more buffs and protection.

recommendedTeams.name: Chevreuse Mono-Pyro Lyney Team
notes: Chevreuse replaces Anemo supports for Lyney triple-Pyro mono team as she gives him ATK buffs and Pyro RES reduction. Your Electro character can be any off-fielders or buffer supports, but we recommend slower Electro or faster Pyro application for Lyney's passive to work.

recommendedTeams.name: Chevreuse Overloaded Free-to-Play Teams
notes: If you're looking for F2P options, Yanfei and Xiangling are usable as the Main DPS for Chevreuse support. Yanfei specifically is ranged, so she can follow-up on enemies launched by the knockback effect of Overloaded.

goalNotes: As a DEF-based Sub-DPS, Chiori wants to max out her DEF at a comfortable level, with 2,000 being a good baseline for her.
The rest of her stats should then go into CRIT stats with an emphasis on CRIT Rate in order for her Elemental Skill to do more damage. CRIT DMG should then be maxed out as far as possible.

recommendedTeams.name: Chiori Mono Geo Teams
notes: Chiori can excel well in a Mono-Geo team, as to utilize her passive and Geo Resonance. The team also contains multiple team members who can generate Geo Constructs, to ensure smoother team rotations.
Chiori mostly utilizes her Elemental Skill in these team comps, ensuring delivering constant Geo Damage Off-Field.

recommendedTeams.name: Chiori Double Geo Teams
notes: An alternative is running her alongside one other geo unit like Albedo and Zhongli who can provide both geo resonance and Geo Constructs that can supplement Chiori's Elemental Skill.
It is important to note that other non-construct Geo units can be used, but their synergy will be limited due to Chiori's DPS being restricted to one Tamoto on the field prior to C1.

recommendedTeams.name: Chiori-Navia Teams
notes: At C1, Chiori can function outside of Mono Geo and Construct-Geo characters, allowing her to pair up with Navia more optimally to enable Geo resonance and produce more Crystallize shards for them, all without stunting Chiori's personal damage.

recommendedTeams.name: Chongyun Freeze and Shatter Team
notes: This Main DPS build for Chongyun can be good for both single target and multiple enemies. Adding an Anemo character to debuff enemies by using the Viridescent Venerer set and to group enemes will be ideal.
Zhongli could be placed in the support slot, just keep his pillar away from the fight to prevent it from stealing shatters.

recommendedTeams.name: Chongyun National Team
notes: Chongyun with Hydro and Pyro party members is a good budget team to mix Elemental Reaction DMG.

recommendedTeams.name: Chongyun Melt Team
notes: This Melt team for Chongyun focuses on triggering Melt Elemental Reaction. Chongyun's Elemental Skill at C2 works very well with Bennett's, making his Elemental Skill have a very short cooldown.

goalNotes: The first priority is to get Citlali's Energy Recharge to at least 180% to ensure that she can use her Elemental Burst off-cooldown regardless of her team placement.
Afterwards, the rest of her stats can be placed into more Elemental Mastery, or even stats like CRIT if you want her to do damage.

recommendedTeams.name: Standard Pyro Melt
notes: One half of Citlali's intended archetype are Melt teams, where she benefits the team from her off-field Cryo application and Pyro RES reduction to enemies.
Depending on Citlali's Cryo Application uptime versus your Pyro Main DPS, Citlali may not be enough as a solo applicator, so you may slot in another Cryo like Rosaria.

recommendedTeams.name: Frozen Melt
notes: As Hydro Characters can also benefit from the RES reduction, including Hydro to freeze the enemies first before your Pyro DPS Melts the Frozen enemy is a viable option to better the Melt frequency.
One big caveat is that teams relying on Frozen cannot efficiently work on Bosses and so the Hydro can be dropped in favor of standard Melt.

recommendedTeams.name: Plunge Melt
notes: Plunge teams with Citlali can have her potentially act as a solo applicator for Cryo so that Plunge DPS like Gaming can time their plunge attack to Melt the enemy.

recommendedTeams.name: Citlali Freeze Teams
notes: Frozen is another viable team comp for Citlali in terms of AoE content if you need another Cryo Applicator who can also act as your defensive support.

goalNotes: Bring Clorinde's ATK to around 1,800 or above, with 2,000 being the ideal due to all of her attacks being ATK-based, then focus on getting her CRIT stats up with a priority on CRIT Rate reaching at least 70%.

Prioritize CRIT DMG and Energy Recharge last, with an emphasis on getting CRIT DMG as high as possible and having spare substats go into Energy Recharge to ensure that she can get her Burst back faster.

recommendedTeams.name: Clorinde Aggravate
notes: Since Dendro and Electro will stick onto the enemy, Clorinde can easily trigger Aggravate DMG with her already enhanced Elemental Skill, leading to her already strong attacks receiving a near-consistent buff.

recommendedTeams.name: Clorinde Overload
notes: Overload has plenty of options that can work well with Clorinde, so she can become a viable Overload DPS due to having good on-field Electro application that can match off-field DMG dealers like Xiangling.

recommendedTeams.name: Clorinde Quickbloom/Hyperbloom
notes: Similar to other Hyperbloom drivers, Clorinde can function as both an on-field DPS that can carry Electro damage, as well as being the Hyperbloom trigger.

recommendedTeams.name: Clorinde Lunar-Charge/Electro-Charge
notes: Clorinde's A1 Passive gives her a decent increase to her damage without the need of standard damage buffers, letting her slot into both Lunar-Charge and Electro-Charge teams as the main damage dealer to great effect, with the former being augmented thanks to Lunar enablers like Columbina.
When paired with 2 Hydro applicators and especially someone like Furina, the team's damage and Electro-Charge's frequency skyrockets, making this one of Clorinde's best teams.

recommendedTeams.name: Clorinde Hypercarry
notes: Clorinde's own damage paired with either more buffs and some form of sustain gives her access to a near solo-onfield hypercarry playstyle to brute force through content.
This is in contrast to her more team-oriented playstyle, trading Elemental Reactions for overwhelming electro damage.

recommendedTeams.name: Collei Burgeon Team

recommendedTeams.name: F2P Collei Team

recommendedTeams.name: Iansan Overload Teams

recommendedTeams.name: Iansan Aggravate Teams
notes: Due to being an Electro unit, Iansan is an eligible member for most Dendro-related teams, especially if the main damage dealer can benefit off Iansan's ATK buffs.

recommendedTeams.name: Iansan Electro-Charge Teams
notes: As an Electro unit, Iansan is also able to facilitate Electro-Charge procs with her Elemental Skill, but still mostly serves as a buffer in these teams.

recommendedTeams.name: Iansan Superconduct Teams
notes: Due to Iansan's buffs being ATK-based, she can specifically aid Superconduct teams as most of their carries scale off the ATK stat.

recommendedTeams.name: Ifa Electro-Charge Teams
notes: Ifa is mainly placed as the On-Field Anemo Driver for Electro-Charge teams due to his ability to keep the team sustained while increasing the damage of the party.
Ororon in particular is one of his best allies as he fulfills half the team requirement for Electro-Charge, as well as possessing Nightsoul's Blessing.

recommendedTeams.name: Ifa Hyperbloom Teams
notes: With Hyperbloom teams also containing possible Electro-Charge procs, Ifa can facilitate many of the possible reactions that happen, treating this team as a possible sidegrade of Electro-Charge.

goalNotes: As a dedicated Elemental Mastery Support, Illuga wants his Elemental Mastery to be as high as possible while keeping up Energy Recharge requirements to use his Burst off-cooldown, as that is most of his contribution.
Optionally, get your CRIT Rate up to around 40 ~ 50% if using Favonius Lance to reliably proc the Energy regeneration passive.

recommendedTeams.name: Illuga-Zibai Teams
notes: Zibai is especially appreciative of Illuga's buffing capabilities for Lunar-Crystallize, making them a tandem when it comes to Zibai's teams.
Illuga contributes a lot to Zibai’s damage, but he is not a hard requirement for the latter to function.

recommendedTeams.name: General Lunar-Crystallize Teams
notes: Illuga can still fight right into general Lunar-Crystallize, but he must be paired with Columbina to make use of his entire kit, Lunar reactions, and Ascendant Gleam.
Take note that the output of this team is significantly less without a dedicated Lunar-Crystallize DPS.

goalNotes: As mentioned, Ineffa only needs to reach 2000 ATK to max out her passive talent requirements. You will need to balance CRIT Rate, CRIT DMG, and Elemental Mastery afterwards.
You can also stack as much Energy Recharge as you can get, but it will lower the requirements if you're running two Electro characters in the party.

recommendedTeams.name: Ineffa Lunar-Charged Sub-DPS Teams
notes: Ineffa teams with Hydro or Electro carriers like Neuvillette and Clorinde can utilize Ineffa's off-field Electro application to contribute to the Lunar-Charged DMG Ineffa creates. For Hydro Application, Yelan and Furina are the premiere appliers, although you can also use Xingqiu if they're not available.
For the last team slot, if you need healing for your Furina, then Xilonen is best to round it up, otherwise you can run Kazuha to also Swirl the reaction to all enemies.

recommendedTeams.name: Ineffa Lunar-Charged Swirl Teams
notes: On teams focused on Swirl on-fielders like Ifa and Mizuki, if run with Furina, they can also run another Hydro or Electro Sub-DPS like Yelan, Ororon, or Fischl.

recommendedTeams.name: Ineffa Lunar-Charged Hyperbloom Teams
notes: Outside of Lunar-Charged, as Hydro and Electro status can still coexist on the enemy, you can add a Dendro character to create an alternate Hyperbloom team.
As much as possible, try only slotting one Dendro or two Hydro characters as having too much Dendro application might interfere with the reaction.

recommendedTeams.name: Jahoda Lunar-Charged Teams

recommendedTeams.name: Jean - Furina Team Comp

recommendedTeams.name: Sunfire Team Comp

recommendedTeams.name: Kachina Rainbow Teams

recommendedTeams.name: Kachina Double Geo Teams

recommendedTeams.name: Kachina Mono Geo Teams

recommendedTeams.name: Kaeya Freeze Hypercarry Teams

recommendedTeams.name: Kaeya Superconduct Teams

Kaeya is best used in this team comp for off-field damage, constant application of Cryo, and provding Energy for Shenhe.

recommendedTeams.name: Kaeya Freeze Teams
notes: Kaeya in Freeze team comp provides the set-up for swirling Freeze and buffing Cryo with Kazuha. Ayaka, or your Cryo Main DPS, will then utilize the buffs. In addition, Kaeya's spammable Elemental Skill can provide much needed Energy for Ayaka.

recommendedTeams.name: Kaeya Dendro Fridge Teams

recommendedTeams.name: Kaveh Lunar-Bloom

recommendedTeams.name: Kaveh Bloom Teams

If you don't have Nilou, you can also slot in Xingqiu, Kokomi, or Ayato for their off-field Hydro application.

recommendedTeams.name: Kaveh Hyperbloom Teams

recommendedTeams.name: Kaveh Burgeon Teams
notes: Similar to Bloom teams, Kaveh can drive Burgeon teams as he can mitigate the damage from the explosions due to his healing passive. Slot-in a strong Hydro applicator like Xingqiu and another Dendro to prevent Vaporize or Burning.

recommendedTeams.name: Kaveh Spread Teams
notes: If you wish to build Kaveh as the carry of the team, you will have to make use of the Spread reaction. Note that Spread + Hyperbloom is still the superior choice as Kaveh's base DMG on his Normal and Charged Attacks aren't as high to be used alone.

recommendedTeams.name: Kaveh Spread Plunge Teams
notes: Kaveh, by virtue of being a Claymore character, can work with Xianyun to serve as a Plunge DPS utilizing a reaction like Spread.

Since Xianyun is able to buff the damage of Plunge attacks, it places the damage ceiling slightly higher than a normal Spread team, which makes this a viable choice for players who want to use Kaveh as a more traditional DPS.

recommendedTeams.name: Kazuha Freeze Teams

recommendedTeams.name: Kazuha Main DPS Buffer Teams

Note that Sucrose can achieve a similar role if the team prefers her Elemental Mastery buffs.

recommendedTeams.name: Kazuha Mixed Teams
notes: Because Kazuha builds Elemental Mastery and can buff two elements at the same time, mixed team comps that can trigger two Elemental Reactions at the same time like Electro-Charged and Overload are good as it can increase his personal and the team's overall DMG.

recommendedTeams.name: Kazuha Main DPS Teams
notes: With the addition of Faruzan and Furina into the game, Main DPS Kazuha has become more viable due to his high damage scalings being driven higher by these supports, with C6 completely unlocking this playstyle.
This allows Kazuha to function as either the Main Anemo DPS when supported by Faruzan, or as an Anemo DPS/Driver hybrid when paired with other DPS units.

recommendedTeams.name: Aggravate Team Comp

recommendedTeams.name: Electro Charged Team Comp
notes: This Electro Charged team comp can be used to tase enemies who can't be frozen. You can opt to choose any Electro or Hydro unit that can provide off field Elemental DMG and give you buffs at the same time.

goalNotes: Kinich's main priority is to get his ATK to around 2,000 or more, and then his CRIT Rate to 40 - 50% as that will scale to 80 - 90% while under the effects of Obsidian Codex's 4-pc. passive.
The rest of his stats go into CRIT DMG, taking it as far as you can go to increase the damage of his Elemental Skill.

recommendedTeams.name: Kinich Burning Teams
notes: Burning teams are one half of Kinich's intended team comps as his kit wants him to attack enemies who are currently in the Burning (or Burgeon) state to gain more Nightsoul points, while also benefitting allies like Emilie who both synergize well for this particular niche.

You may opt on using any off-field Pyro like Xiangling, Thoma, or Dehya as long as the Burning Aura doesn't fall off. Emilie is not required for Burning teams, so you may also use other Dendro supports like Nahida, Baizhu, or Collei for the Deepwood Memories effect coverage.
With the release of Nicole, she is now part for most of Kinich's best team because of the utility and buffs that she provides.

recommendedTeams.name: Kinich Burgeon Teams
notes: Burgeon teams are the other half of Kinich's intended team composition to accumulate Nightsoul points, utilizing at least one Hydro and Pyro. Thoma or Dehya are the best Pyro off-field characters you can use, as they provide slow off-field application as well as shields to protect you against the Burgeon explosions.

recommendedTeams.name: Kinich Quicken Teams
notes: You may also use Kinich on Quicken teams with an Electro character just as fine as a Dendro carry, but do note that Kinich gains less Nighstoul points from not having a Burning or Burgeon reaction occur in the field, which leads to him shooting less Scalespiker Cannons for lesser damage overall.

recommendedTeams.name: Kinich Quickbloom Teams
notes: Kinich can also function in a Quickbloom team as the Dendro applicator, allowing him to generate bloom cores for use by the Electro trigger.

One thing to keep track of is that his Elemental Skill puts him at range against an opponent, and sometimes an Electro trigger like Shinobu needs to be close to trigger bloom cores, and cannot do so if Kinich is sliding too much away from the source.

goalNotes: Kirara shield stacks with her HP, making 35,000 HP or higher the goal point for it as that provides Kirara a healthy Shield that does not easily break.
As a general rule of thumb, Kirara's Energy Recharge should be around 160% on average as that will allow her to use her Elemental Burst almost every rotation.

recommendedTeams.name: Kirara in Bloom Teams
notes: In Nilou Bloom team comps, Kirara can effectively minimize Bloom DMG taken with her shields as a Support, and she can also act as the driver to apply Dendro with her Hold Elemental Skill as a Sub-DPS.

Xingqiu's swords ring that surround the active character can also apply Hydro when Kirara touches enemies, but Xingqiu will need Elemental Mastery as he will most likely be the one triggering the Bloom Cores.
You will need some Elemental Mastery on Kirara as she can trigger cores as well.

recommendedTeams.name: Kirara Hyperbloom Teams
notes: These Kirara teams prioritize triggering Hyperbloom reactions with her as a Support, with her both providing protection and Dendro application for your party members.

recommendedTeams.name: Kirara Aggravate/Spread Teams
notes: Kirara can take over Zhongli or Baizhu in Quicken teams as a support, and can provide backup as a Dendro enabler. If you need healing, Fischl can be replaced with Shinobu or other healers to replace damage for comfort.

recommendedTeams.name: Kirara Burgeon Team
notes: Slotting Kirara in Burgeon teams can minimize self inflicted DMG from Burgeon DMG. You can also on-field swap to her if you need her Elemental Skill while there's downtime.

recommendedTeams.name: Xiangling-Bennett Duo Teams
notes: Together with Bennett, Xiangling fits into a variety of teams that make use of her high-frequency Pyro application, creating a feedback loop of constant transformative damage with characters like Tartaglia, Wriothesley, Neuvillette, and Raiden.

recommendedTeams.name: Xiangling Overload Teams
notes: Xiangling can also be paired with someone like Chevreuse, letting her slot into Overload teams easily with her high Pyro application.

recommendedTeams.name: Xiangling Burning Teams
notes: Xiangling can also function as the Pyro element upkeeper in burn teams, often paired with units like Emilie or Nahida to facilitate burning damage, then to characters like Alhaitham and Arlecchino who can extend it, or characters like Wriothesley and Lohen who can do amplified damage off of it.

goalNotes: Xianyun wants to get as much attack as possible, with the maximum being 4,500. To that end, getting ATK values around 3,500 - 4,000 is enough for her supportive capabilities.
Lastly, she wants to reach around 200% ER in general to get her Elemental Burst back off-cooldown.

recommendedTeams.name: Xianyun - Varesa Premium Team
notes: Xianyun complements Varesa, who is currently the best low-investment Plunge Attacker in the game. You can run her with a Hypercarry teams with Iansan alongside either Furina or Xilonen, depending on your team needs.

recommendedTeams.name: Xianyun Vaporize or Melt Teams
notes: Teams with characters who can benefit from Xianyun's plunging utility and healing in tandem with Furina's buffs are her best teams for Viridescent Venerer teams.
Vaporize is one such team comp. We recommend having a Main DPS that have high plunging attack scalings like Diluc, who also benefits from reactions with Hydro, are good to slot-in.
Gaming, like Xiao, also plays around plunging attacks, and it is expected that they will pair well together. You may also play around Melt by having off-field applicators like Rosaria and Layla.

recommendedTeams.name: Xianyun - Xiao Premium Team
notes: Xiao's kit is designed around using Plunging Attacks. With Xianyun, his damage gets a big boost thanks to her. This team uses Song of Days Past for Xianyun.

Xianyun and Xiao also synergize well with Furina, as the former can replenish the party's HP, and the latter can decrease his own by himself. Having Faruzan in this team, especially at C6, maximizes the damage you can possibly have for him!

recommendedTeams.name: Xianyun Other Plunge Teams
notes: All Claymore characters tend to have high Plunging Attack modifiers than most weapon types, so as long as they can infuse themselves with their own element, they are all viable as your Main DPS enabled by Xianyun.

recommendedTeams.name: Xianyun Main DPS Team
notes: Xianyun as a Main DPS will act as a Hypercarry Driver, so you will need one Anemo Support, and other buffers like Furina and Bennett. You can also mix in other Sub-DPS like Fischl or Xiangling if you want to play as a Swirl driver, although you will want Elemental Mastery.

recommendedTeams.name: Xianyun Free-to-Play Team
notes: Most of Xianyun's best team comps consist with Furina in mind. If you don't have her, you may use the usual characters who can apply elements or buff your party members like Xingqiu, Bennett, Sucrose, or Xiangling.
Gaming can be obtained for free in the 2024 Lantern Rite, so if you want to use him with Xianyun, using Vaporize is one of his best teams!

recommendedTeams.name: Plunging Team with Faruzan and Xianyun
notes: Faruzan is a welcome addition to Xiao's party thanks to her Anemo DMG buffs. If Faruzan is below C6, you may need another Anemo character like Jean or Sucrose to fill up Xiao's energy easily.

Furina and Xianyun can further boost Xiao's damage for plunging playstyles, as well as provide off-field damage, but if you don't have Xianyun or Furina, you may use Zhongli, Jean, or Bennett as well.

recommendedTeams.name: Double Anemo & Double Geo Team
notes: This team comp synergizes well with keeping Xiao safe as he deals damage with his Elemental Burst. Jean will provide particle generation for Xiao's Elemental burst and can also increase his DPS if she has her 4th Constellation unlocked.

recommendedTeams.name: Xiao Free-to-Play Team Comp
notes: As his best teams are rather expensive, you can use 4-star characters like Bennett and Sucrose as alternatives. Sucrose's Elemental Mastery buffs won't really work for Xiao, but she does provide a lot of energy especially with a Favonius Codex and constellations.

goalNotes: At the very least, Xilonen wants at least 190% Energy Recharge to nearly get her Elemental Burst up with one use of her Elemental Skill. Afterwards, getting her DEF as high as you can is your next priority.
Somewhere around 2,500 minimum is enough to utilize a good portion of her buffs, with 3,000 being the standard if you have her Signature Weapon.

recommendedTeams.name: Xilonen Hypercarry Teams
notes: Xilonen can specifically team up with one elemental Main DPS, Furina, and Kazuha in order to serve as both the healer and one of the three buffers in the team.

Unlike most team comps, this team puts absolute focus on enhancing the raw damage coming from the Main DPS as much as possible, bypassing any setup or reaction in favor of straightforward and strong damage.

recommendedTeams.name: Xilonen Vaporize Teams
notes: Xilonen can fulfill the buffer role in Vaporize teams, being able to constantly shred the Pyro and Hydro RES of enemies without interrupting elemental reactions due to her low Geo application.
This makes her especially effective in Vaporize teams where Hydro cannot consistently be swirled by someone like Kazuha, as she bypasses the need for proper set-up entirely.

recommendedTeams.name: Xilonen Melt/Freeze Teams
notes: Freeze teams often suffer from a low damage ceiling, which is something that Xilonen can remedy by taking on the role of both healer and buffer, allowing the team to slot in another damage-oriented unit.
She is also able to consistently buff both Cryo and Hydro, and can even be paired with Shenhe in order to skyrocket the amount of Cryo damage that the team can output.

recommendedTeams.name: Xilonen Mono Teams
notes: In mono elemental teams, Xilonen is able to buff all the characters involved in the team, as all of them are likely to come from the same element.
She can also run these teams with another buffer in order to augment the team's overall damage even more, especially if their Main and Sub DPS units already have enough damage on their own.

recommendedTeams.name: Xilonen Navia Teams
notes: Xilonen fulfills the role of buffer and Geo Resonance partner for Navia, as slotting her in Navia's premium Pyro team allows Navia to take advantage of Pyro Resonance, Geo Resonance, and the default Geo RES shred from Xilonen.

These array of buffs also extend to any elemental Sub-DPS that the team has due to Xilonen's RES shred, making them more formidable while still being able to contribute to Navia's crystallize reactions without interruption.

goalNotes: Xingqiu's main stat priority is his Energy Recharge, as having around 180% ER lets him recharge his Elemental Burst with two Elemental Skill usages.
Afterwards, to ensure that Xingqiu's damage remains respectable, bring him up to a healthy 1:2 CRIT Ratio where he has 60 - 70% CRIT Rate, any amount of CRIT DMG above 120%, and at least 1,800 ATK.

recommendedTeams.name: Xingqiu Vaporize Teams
notes: Xingqiu's frequent Hydro application lets him slot well into Vaporize teams, where he enables the Main Pyro DPS to hit enemies for amplified damage.
He is usually also paired with another Hydro unit like Yelan as that double-downs on the Vaporize reaction's DPS.

recommendedTeams.name: Xingqiu Hyperbloom Teams
notes: Xingqiu's Hydro application is often enough to function as the sole Hydro applicator in a Hyperbloom team, and performs well due to both the frequency of his application and the damage reduction from his Elemental Burst.

recommendedTeams.name: Xingqiu Electro-Charged Teams
notes: In Electro-Charged teams, Xingqiu helps provide Electro-Charge procs to enemies with his abilities as they hone in on them at frequent intervals.
This is also often amplified by the presence of a buffer Anemo unit like Kazuha or Sucrose.

recommendedTeams.name: Xingqiu Freeze Teams
notes: Due to the overwhelming amount of Cryo in Freeze teams, Xingqiu's Hydro Application is usually sought after since it can keep enemies Frozen and keep them from harming the team.

goalNotes: Regardless of your build, Yae Miko normally wants around 2,000 ATK or more to capitalize off her own raw damage, with Energy Recharge at around 130~140% at least to help charge her Elemental Burst.
Afterwards, focus on 60~70% CRIT Rate to capitalize on the frequent Off-Field damage she provides, and as much CRIT DMG as you can add.

recommendedTeams.name: Dendro Teams
notes: Pretty much, Yae Miko can work in any team that has a Dendro presence, allowing her to proc Aggravate and/or Hyperbloom if the situation allows for it, though the latter is less recommended due to Yae Miko wanting ATK most of the time. She will most often be paired with Dendro staples like Alhaitham and Nahida due to her own abundance of Electro.

recommendedTeams.name: Yanfei Overloaded Team
notes: Yanfei can also lead an Overloaded team, but you will need Chevreuse for this specific team comp for her Pyro Damage increase from her passive.

recommendedTeams.name: Yanfei Burn Team
notes: With the addition of units like Nahida and Emilie, Burning teams become a viable option for Yanfei due to the consistent burn damage she can cause, as well as the supportive Sub-DPS damage from their Dendro partner.

recommendedTeams.name: Yanfei Burgeon Team
notes: With her AoE capabilities, Yanfei can lead a Burgeon team, as long as Nahida applies Dendro first then followed by Xingqiu's Hydro application to secure a Dendro core.
Keep in mind that Yanfei needs to be built around stacking Elemental Mastery as much as possible for this to amplify Burgeon Damage.

recommendedTeams.name: Yaoyao Spread Team
notes: Spread Teams focus on creating Quicken reactions followed by Dendro DMG. Dendro DPS characters like Alhaitham, Nahida, and Tighnari will benefit from increased Dendro DMG and healing from Yaoyao.

recommendedTeams.name: Yaoyao Aggravate Team
notes: Aggravate Teams focus on creating Quicken reactions followed by Electro application to increase overall Electro DMG. Electro characters like Cyno, Keqing, and Fischl will benefit from increased Electro DMG from Aggravate and healing from Yaoyao.

recommendedTeams.name: Yaoyao Hyperbloom Team
notes: This Yaoyao team focuses on the Hyperbloom reaction. Along with Yaoyao, you must have at least one Hydro and one Electro character to create Dendro Cores and the Hyperbloom reaction respectively.
Raiden and Shinobu are perfect Hyperbloom triggers as they can periodically deal AoE Electro damage while off-field to hit Dendro Cores.

recommendedTeams.name: Yaoyao Burgeon Team
notes: This Yaoyao team focuses on the Burgeon reaction. Along with Yaoyao, you must have at least one Hydro and one Pyro character to create Dendro Cores and the Burgeon reaction respectively.
Yaoyao is an essential member of the Burgeon team as the reaction can also damage your active character.

recommendedTeams.name: Yelan Freeze Teams
notes: With Frozen becoming more of a prevalent Elemental Reaction, Yelan has gained traction as one of the units that can keep up with freeze teams, being able to provide both her own personal damage and a teamwide Elemental DMG Bonus.

recommendedTeams.name: Yelan and Nilou Bountiful Core Team
Yelan Vaporize Team
notes: Yelan in this Sub-DPS team comp teams up with Xingqiu to provide a lot of Hydro for Hu Tao to trigger Vaporize. Yelan not only provides Hydro application, but also having the added benefit of increasing Hu Tao's DMG!

recommendedTeams.name: Yelan International Team
notes: This classic team replaces Xingqiu with Yelan as the character who hails from Liyue. What's great about this build is that Yelan can provide amazing DPS while Raiden's Elemental Burst is on cooldown.

recommendedTeams.name: Yelan Electro-Charged Team
notes: Yelan can act as an on-field or off-field unit in an Electro-Charged team comp. Electro-Charged teams still does very good damage in the current meta, given how much reactions are triggered during rotations.

recommendedTeams.name: Yoimiya Reverse-Vaporize Team
notes: Yoimiya's main mode of operation are her Reverse-Vaporize teams where she can take advantage of Hydro units to constantly hit Vaporized shots.
Most teams have Yoimiya as the sole main damage dealer, meaning she would also benefit from defensive options or buffs.

recommendedTeams.name: Yoimiya Melt Teams
notes: Yoimiya can also function well in Melt Teams as the Main DPS, especially when paired with strong Off-Field Cryo units like Rosaria and Citlali.

recommendedTeams.name: Yoimiya Overloaded Team
notes: This Yoimiya team comp focuses on dealing damage through Overloaded, but you will need Chevreuse for this specific team comp. You may also use Bennett to add more buffs for Yoimiya.

recommendedTeams.name: Yoimiya Reverse-Vaporize Anemo Team
notes: This Anemo Reverse Vaporize team will have Kazuha absorb Hydro in his Elemental Burst. After, swap to Thoma to apply pyro with his Elemental Burst and then swap back to Kazuha to use his Elemental Skill to Swirl Pyro. This is to ensure Yoimiya gets full Pyro Buffs from Kazuha's Viridescent Venerer Set.

recommendedTeams.name: Yoimiya Reverse-Vaporize F2P Team
notes: This is a more free to play friendly team for Yoimiya's ideal team comp. Yun Jin can be replaced with Bennett if you need her somewhere else. This build also works wonders if you have Thoma at C6.

recommendedTeams.name: Yun Jin & Ayato Team
notes: Ayato can also benefit from Yun Jin as he also specializes in Normal Attacks. The Normal Attack buff from Yun Jin combined with Pyro application for Vaporize will help deal tons of DMG.

recommendedTeams.name: Yun Jin & Noelle Team
notes: Noelle and Yun Jin can have some variety in their team combos. With the introduction of Furina, Noelle can be boosted by both Furina and Yun Jin into new heights.
Yun Jin and Gorou can provide DMG buffs to Noelle while Fischl can deal supplementary Electro DMG and provide a lot of energy particles.

recommendedTeams.name: Yun Jin & Wanderer Team
notes: Wanderer can be especially supported by Yun Jin due to both her Normal Attack buffs. This fully complements Wanderer due to his main source of damage being his Normal Attacks.
At C6, this duo becomes even more potent with Yun Jin increasing Wanderer's Attack Speed, therefore increasing the amount of damage he can do during his Elemental Skill.

recommendedTeams.name: Hypercarry Teams

goalNotes: Similar to most Nod-Krai DPS units, Zibai wants to have a healthy amount of DEF and CRIT stats to deal heavy damage with her Empowered Elemental Skill, so these should be focused first.
Elemental Mastery is welcome as that supplements her Lunar-Crystallize DMG, and Energy Recharge can be great as excess substats if you are looking to use her Elemental Burst more often.

recommendedTeams.name: Zibai Premium Lunar-Crystallize Teams
notes: Lunar-Crystallize is her best-case scenario in team building, as her entire playstyle centers around it. Having a Moonsign character along is an added benefit that allows her to have access to her Ascendant Gleam, dealing an additional Lunar-Crystallize DMG on her Normal Attack string.
Linnea and/or Columbina are her premier supports as they can easily increase the Lunar-Crystallize DMG that Zibai unleashes during her rotation.

recommendedTeams.name: Zibai F2P Lunar-Crystallize Teams
notes: Not many options are going on with the F2P teams, but nonetheless, they're still viable. As per the standard, you’d want to pair Zibai with Hydro and Geo units in order to trigger her Lunar-Reaction.
Aino and Jahoda are great Moonsign characters to pair her with, but be mindful of Jahoda's gameplay as she takes a lot of field time to function.
